idea.body: A mixed number is a whole number plus a fraction, like 2 3/4. To convert an improper fraction to a mixed number, divide the top by the bottom. 11/4 is 11 divided by 4, which is 2 remainder 3. So 11/4 = 2 3/4. To go the other way, multiply the whole number by the bottom number, then add the top number, and keep the same bottom number. 2 3/4 becomes (2 x 4) + 3 = 11, over 4, giving 11/4. Adding or subtracting mixed numbers works on the whole numbers and fraction parts separately. The exception is when the fraction parts add past one whole, or the second fraction is bigger than the first. Then a whole number moves across: carrying or borrowing.

figure.alt: A stack of 2 full bars plus one partial bar with 3 out of 4 shaded, showing 11/4 as 2 3/4.

workedExample.prompt: A garden bed has 2 3/4 rows planted. A second bed adds 1 1/2 more rows. How many rows are planted in total?
steps: The fraction parts have different bottom numbers, so give them both bottom number 4: 3/4 stays, and 1/2 becomes 2/4.
Add the fraction parts: 3/4 + 2/4 = 5/4, which is more than one whole.
5/4 is 1 whole and 1/4 left over, so carry that extra whole into the whole number total: 3 + 1 = 4.

figure.alt: A stack of 4 full bars plus one partial bar with 1 out of 4 shaded, showing the carried result 4 1/4.

ways.name: Add the parts separately, then carry
ways.when: Use this when adding or subtracting two mixed numbers directly.
steps: Add the whole numbers first: 2 plus 1 is 3.
Give the fraction parts the same bottom number: 3/4 stays, and 1/2 becomes 2/4.
Add the fraction parts: 3/4 plus 2/4 is 5/4, which is more than one whole.
5/4 is 1 whole and 1/4 left over, so carry that whole into the total: 3 plus 1 is 4.
ways.trap: Forgetting to carry a whole number across when the fraction parts add past one whole.

figure.alt: A stack of 4 full bars plus one partial bar with 1 out of 4 shaded, showing the carried result 4 and 1 quarter.

ways.name: Turn both into improper fractions
ways.when: Use this when carrying or borrowing feels confusing to track by hand.
steps: Convert each mixed number to an improper fraction: 2 3/4 becomes 11/4, since 2 x 4 plus 3 is 11.
Convert 1 1/2 to fourths too: 1 1/2 is 3/2, which becomes 6/4.
Add the improper fractions: 11/4 plus 6/4 is 17/4.
Convert back to a mixed number: 17 divided by 4 is 4 remainder 1, giving 4 1/4.
ways.trap: Forgetting to rewrite the second fraction's bottom number to match before adding.

ways.name: Hop along a number line
ways.when: Use this when subtracting and it helps to see the moves.
steps: Start at 3 1/3 on the number line.
Hop back 1 whole number first: land at 2 1/3.
Now hop back the fraction part, 2/3: since 1/3 is smaller than 2/3, borrow a whole as 3/3, making 1/3 into 4/3.
Hop back 2/3 from 1 and 4/3: 4/3 minus 2/3 is 2/3, landing at 1 2/3.
ways.trap: Hopping back the fraction part before the whole number, and forgetting to borrow when it is too small.

figure.alt: A number line from 0 to 4 showing three hops: 3 and 1 third, then 2 and 1 third, then 1 and 2 thirds.
